DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 98 s. 2021 MEMORANDUM TO SUBJECT DATE DIR. PAISAL O. ABUTAZIL Regional Director, DILG-Region IX President Corazon C. Aquino Regional Government Center Brgy. Balintawak, Pagadian City VERY URGENT REQUEST FOR LEGAL OPINION FROM PD MOH TAHA S. ARAKAMA, DILG ZAMBOANGA DEL SUR RE KUMALARANG CASE 26 July 2021 Reference: Your Memorandum dated July 22, 2021 requesting a definite legal opinion on the matter to prevent disruption in the operation of the concerned local government unit. Per the documents forwarded to the Central Office, on July 08, 2021 , the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Zamboanga del Sur adopted Resolution No. 1509-2021 entitled "RECOMMENDING TO THE HONORABLE VICTOR J. YU, PROVINCIAL GOVERNOR OF THE PROVINCE OF ZAMBOANGA DEL SUR, FOR THE ISSUANCE OF A 60-DAY PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION ORDER AGAINST MUNICIPAL MAYOR RUEL G. MOLINA OF THE MUNICIPALITY OF KUMALARANG, RESPONDENT IN ADMINISTRATIVE CASE NO. SP-1-2021, ENTITLED 'HON. RANIEL GRACIANO O. DORMITORIO, ET AL., COMPLAINANTS, VS. HON. RUEL G. MOLINA, RESPONDENT FOR ABUSE OF AUTHORITY AND MISCONDUCT IN OFFICE". The said Resolution was received by the Office of the Governor on July 9, 2021. On July 19, 2021 , Governor Yu issued an Order placing Mayor Ruel G. Molina under preventive suspension. On the same day, Mayor Molina was able to secure a 72-hour Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) issued by the Executive Judge of the Regional Trial Court, 9th Judicial Region in Pagadian City. The dispositive portion of the aforesaid TRO reads: "WHEREFORE, finding petitioner's application for a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) effective for Seventy Two (72) hours from issue to be impressed with merit, the same is hereby GRANTED. ENJOINING and "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

RESTRAINING respondent Sangguniang Panglalawigan of the Province of Zamboanga del Sur, represented by Vice Governor Roseller L. Ariosa, Raniel Graciano O. Dormitorio, Jobert C. Dahunan, and Manuel B. Biaco, from acting upon Private Respondents' Ex-Parte Motion for Issuance of Preventive Suspension Order or from enforcing its recommendation if one has already been issued or from conducting any further proceedings in the administrative case, and from rendering any resolution or decision thereon." However, on July 21, 2021, the suspension order was served upon the respondents as evidenced by the Affidavit of Service of Glendell I Oyo-a. On July 22, 2021 , the RTC issued an Order extending the TRO for a period of 17 days. The dispositive portion of said Order reads: "WHEREFORE, in light of the foregoing discussion, the Temporary restraining Order issued per Order of this Court dated 19 July 2021 is hereby extended for a period of seventeen (17) days from 22 July 2021. As stated earlier this has to be amended. Consequently, the Respondents Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the Province of Zamboanga del sur is hereby ENJOINED and RESTRAINED from acting upon the subject Ex-parte Motion for Issuance of Preventive Suspension Order or from enforcing its recommendation if one has already been issued for a period for another 17 days from July 22, 2021. xxxx" It was also highlighted in the TRO that: "xxxx if indeed the Governor has already issued the preventive suspension despite the absence of the recommendation from the Sangguniang Panlalawigan is already beside the point and is not within the confine of this court to take cognizance considering that the Governor is not party to this case. There would be a complete denial of due process if the Governor will be included in the Restraining Order since he is not impleaded in the very place in this case." On the same date, DILG-Zamboanga del Sur received a letter dated July 22, 2021 from the counsel of Mayor Molina requesting that definite actions be taken directing the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Zamboanga del Sur to respect the Court and comply with its legal obligation under the Order, with further request for said Sanggunian and Page 2 of 5

the Office of the Provincial Director to be sanctioned if necessary for the flagrant violation of the previous T RO. In a letter dated July 22, 2021, Vice-Mayor Ranniel Graciano Dormitorio informed DILG-Zamboanga del Sur that he has taken his Oath of Office as Acting Mayor of the Municipality of Kumalarang and at the same time, requested that a Certificate of Recognition be issued to his favor. In a letter dated 22 July 2021, Provincial Director Moh Taha S. Arakama, DILG- Zamboanga del Sur, requested for a legal opinion on the following issues: 1. Whether the TRO issued by the court binds the Provincial Governor who was not impleaded as a party defendant; 2. Whether the said Governor can be bound by a TRO issued on July 19, 2021 enjoining and restraining the said Sanggunian from enforcing its recommendation when it was transmitted as early as July 09, 2021; and 3. Whether the concerned Provincial Director can issue a Certificate of Recognition to Vice Mayor Raniel Graciano O. Dormitorio as Acting Municipal Mayor. As a general rule, the Department is proscribed by its internal rules as provided in DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 to act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: 1. Those containing facts that are justifiable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given controversy; 2. Those presumptively valid acts; e.g., enacted ordinance, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; 3. Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself, requests for opinion. In the event that the opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or the information that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective; and 4. Those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government." For this reason, considering that the case is already pending in court, this Department is of the considered view that these are matters of fact that need to be adjudicated in the proper forum. Page 3 of 5

In view thereof, this Department is constrained from issuing a legal opinion regarding the matter in view of the sub judice rule which means that when a legal matter or controversy has come under the jurisdiction of a court (sub judice), nobody, should interfere by publication or public clamor with the court's proper handling of the proceeding. At any rate, for purposes of academic discussion coupled with our objective to guide the concerned on the proper course of action to take under the prevailing circumstances, we deem it necessary to indulge in disquisition on the laws/ case law applicable on the matter. On the first and second queries, it is our humble submission that Governor Yu, as a non-impleaded party, is not covered by the TRO issued by the Regional Trial Court (RTC) of Pagadian City. The case filed by Mayor Molina was a Special Civil Action for Prohibition/lnjunction with Application for Preliminary Prohibitory Injunction and Temporary Restraining Order (T RO). It is a personal action where the impleaded respondent was only the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the Province of Zamboanga, as represented by Vice-Govemor Roseller Ariosa, Raniel Graciano Dormitorio, Jobert Dahunan and Manuel Biaco. There is no quibbling that as a provisional remedy to prevent irreparable injury pending the final determination of the action, injunction can bind only the parties in the action, or their privies or successors-in-interest. No person who has not been impleaded and duly served with the summons should be adversely affected by the outcome of the action (Power Sector Assets And Liabilities Management Corporation (Psalm), vs. Court Of Appeals (21st Division), and Francisco Labao, G.R. No. 194226, Feb. 15, 2017). Moreover, Section I, Rule 58 of the Rules of Court clarifies the foregoing point in the following provision: "Section 1. Preliminary injunction defined; classes. — A preliminary iniunction is an order granted at any stage of an action or proceedinq prior to the iudqment or final order. reguiring a party or a court. agency or a person to refrain from a particular act or acts. It may also require the performance of a particular act or acts, in which case it shall be known as a preliminary mandatory injunction." (Emphasis Supplied) We note, however, that in the July 19, 2021 RTC Order, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Zamboanga del Sur was refrained from doing following acts: I) Acting upon Private Respondents' Ex-Parte Motion for Issuance of Preventive Suspension Order, 2) Or, from enforcing its recommendation if one has already been issued, 3) Or, from conducting any further proceedings in the administrative case, and 4) From rendering any resolution or decision thereon. Page 4 of 5

Further, the Court in its Order dated July 22, 2021 extended the TRO for seventeen (17) more days and emphasized its reservation on the propriety of preventively suspending Mayor Molina. The Court reasoned, as supported by jurisprudence, that preventive suspension may only be imposed before the complainants in the administrative case shall have rested their case as a way of preventing the respondent from exerting undue influence or pressure on the witnesses against him. In this case, the complainants have already presented their witnesses against the respondent Mayor and the possibility of intimidating witnesses against him is already nil. In other words, the evil sought to be avoided in imposing preventive suspension according to the Court is no longer existing. Hence, the filing of the ex-pane motion for issuance of Preventive Suspension Order or even its implementation is no longer called for at least for the duration of the T RO. As for possible tampering of records, the Court likewise said that the same is no longer tenable as some documentary evidence in this case have already been checked/audited by COA leaving no room for petitioner (Mayor Molina) to tamper them. Ergo, it is the Department's submission that Even if Governor Yu was not impleaded as one of the parties, he should have at least desisted from imposing the suspension of Mayor Molina or caused its holding in abeyance for such period/time that the TRO is existing. As the Court correctly pointed out, the absence of any of the basis for preventive suspension (there are only three under the law) renders its imposition irregular and makes a case for abuse of authority (Sec. 63, (d) of R.A. 7160). Unless this is done, an absurd situation may arise as the reasons for preventive suspension has ceased to exist for the duration of the injunctive relief. As to the third query, this Department will refrain from issuing said Certificate of Recognition based on the foregoing discussion. Aptly, so as not to disrupt local governance in the Municipality of Kumalarang and to ensure that delivery of government services remains uninterrupted, the Department is constrained to recognize the status quo or the last peaceable condition prior to the controversy in the Municipality of Kumalarang, Zamboanga del Sur until such time that the Court's TRO becomes functus officio. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Please be guided accordingly. BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Unders tary for Local Government OSEC/MLI/LLLS Page 5 of 5
